# Vacant

> Vacant is not a mandatory layer wrapped around an AI agent, and it is not another agent
> framework. It is a receiving desk: a delivery without a verifiable receipt is not
> accepted. It looks only at the deliverable and not at how the agent ran, so output from
> any framework can be fed into it. It runs the customer's own
> executable acceptance tests against a candidate, decides ship-or-refuse on the result,
> and signs every attempt — failures included — into an append-only Ed25519 hash chain
> that anyone with the public key can re-verify offline. Install: `pip install vacant-network`
> (import name `vacant`). Python >= 3.11. MIT.

The word is **accountability**, not trust: the classical definitions (Gambetta 1988,
Mayer 1995) make "acting without monitoring" necessary for trust, and monitoring is the
entire content of this system. Do not describe Vacant as a trust layer.

Four things to know before using anything here. (1) **The premise**: the whole mechanism
assumes a requirement can be compiled into an executable acceptance suite; where it
cannot, there is no free referee. (2) **Enforcement is at acceptance time, not execution
time.** The intake check cannot be routed around, but making Vacant the single exit on a
machine takes containers, ACLs or egress policy — the deployment layer's job. In
reference-monitor terms (Saltzer & Schroeder 1975) Vacant is tamper-proof and small
enough to verify, and does **not** satisfy complete mediation. Same pattern as in-toto /
SLSA / Sigstore. (3) **The chain gives integrity, not completeness**: a truncated tail is
a valid prefix and verifies (truncation/omission attack, Ma & Tsudik 2009), and the
checkpoint chain has the same hole. (4) **Passing the acceptance suite is not meeting the
requirement** — measured false delivery is 14.8% even with the gate.

Everything here is meant to be checkable without trusting us: the receipt chains re-verify
offline (`python3 -m vacant_network.vrun.verify_receipts --selftest` runs negative controls first;
in a clone, `ops/gain/replay/verify_run_receipts.py` is the same file),
the task banks are sha256-pinned, and every conclusion can be recounted from
`runs/g_*/rows.jsonl`. That includes our own mistakes: we claimed R532 was "V/GT 43/43
CLEAN" and it was false — the audit tool scanned only the H arm, so the classical seven
arms, `OFF` and `CONFORM` included, were never scanned. The retroactive sweep completed on
2026-09-18 (`ops/gain/vgt_retro_audit_20260918.json`, scope v3 = ten arms, per-arm
fail-closed): 179 archived runs, **165 CLEAN / 10 UNVERIFIABLE / 4 VIOLATION**, 3,486,403
needles checked, with the four cited batches CLEAN on every arm (R460 6/6, R460R 30/30,
R529 37/37, R532 43/43 — the last including R532's 1,122 CONFORM records, audited
dynamically for the first time). The 10 UNVERIFIABLE are aborted runs with no audit target;
the 4 VIOLATION are all in R530 and are the model's own same-named test files, which leaves
whether to tighten that rule **unresolved**. `CLEAN` covers only the literal repr, the bank
is inferred, and the R529/R532 closing analyzers still read the old HMIX-only artifacts.
See `AGENTS.md` §7 H-0 for all of it, boundaries included.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the full machine-facing integration contract — API surface with
  signatures, the four deployment shapes and which are binding, verifiable invariants,
  honest boundaries, common mistakes, and a stable machine-readable facts block.
- [README.md](README.md): human overview in Traditional Chinese — a 30-second offline demo
  of the gate refusing a delivery (`vacant demo gate`), how to wrap your own agent
  (`vacant run -- <cmd>`), and the current results.
  [English](README.en.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md).
- [docs/VACANT_RUN.md](docs/VACANT_RUN.md): `vacant run -- <any agent command>` — what it
  mediates, what it does not, exit codes, on-disk shape, and every honest boundary.
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml): package name, version, and the three runtime dependencies.

## Results and how they were obtained

- [docs/VACANT_COMPLETE_2026-09-12.md](docs/VACANT_COMPLETE_2026-09-12.md): single entry
  point for every number — what exists, what was measured, the honest boundaries, how to
  re-verify it yourself.
- [DECISION_20260912_R460R_FABLE_AUDIT_REPLICATIONS.md](decisions/DECISION_20260912_R460R_FABLE_AUDIT_REPLICATIONS.md):
  five same-task replications, closing audit. The pre-registered claim rule and why the
  result is reported replication-by-replication instead of pooled.
- [DECISION_20260912_R529_FABLE_AUDIT_CROSS_BANK.md](decisions/DECISION_20260912_R529_FABLE_AUDIT_CROSS_BANK.md):
  four mutually exclusive task sets, three real sources, 716 tasks.
- [DECISION_20260917_R532_STRONGER_MODEL_PREREG.md](decisions/DECISION_20260917_R532_STRONGER_MODEL_PREREG.md):
  a different 27B model on 836 tasks, plus two amendments written after seeing the data —
  the state table had no direction guard, and the run's own premise ("a stronger model")
  is not supported by its own data.
- [ops/gain/r532/results_r532.json](ops/gain/r532/results_r532.json): the analyzer's output,
  the citable source for every R532 figure.
- [examples/verdicts.py](examples/verdicts.py): the single source of truth for which
  claims are held, unresolved, overstated, or refuted. Refuted ones are kept, not deleted.
- [runs/INDEX.md](runs/INDEX.md): read before citing any run, task bank, or log — which
  entries are evidence, which are smoke or aborted, and which 136 `_analysis_*`
  directories are derived artefacts that must not be cited as source data.
- [docs/BANKS_HOWTO.md](docs/BANKS_HOWTO.md): how to re-run the task banks yourself.

## Architecture

- [docs/VACANT_ARCHITECTURE_AND_RESULTS_2026-09-07.md](docs/VACANT_ARCHITECTURE_AND_RESULTS_2026-09-07.md): the canonical architecture document.
- [docs/HMIX_ARCHITECTURE_2026-09-11.md](docs/HMIX_ARCHITECTURE_2026-09-11.md): the feedback loop — its six parts, its verbatim prompts, and what it cannot do.
- [docs/HARNESS_STUDY_2026-09-07.md](docs/HARNESS_STUDY_2026-09-07.md): source-level facts about an external harness, and nine folk claims checked one by one.
- [SPEC_GAIN.md](SPEC_GAIN.md): the experiment specification — hidden/visible test separation, fixed task subsets, the definition of each arm.
- [docs/RECORD_SPEC.md](docs/RECORD_SPEC.md): the evidence-pack format.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): working constraints — red lines, terminology, deferred work.
